contents.name: Chapter 4. Fourier coefficients in ell-1(Z) (or f in A(T)) - goal
contents.result: The chapter establishes the algebra structure of A(T).

contents.name: Chapter 4 - definition of A(T)
contents.result: A(T) is the integrable functions with absolutely summable Fourier coefficients.

contents.name: Chapter 4 - uniform Fourier synthesis
contents.result: An ell-1 coefficient sequence gives a uniformly convergent series and continuous representative.

contents.name: Definition 4.1
contents.result: The A(T) norm is the ell-1 coefficient norm and A(T) is complete.

contents.name: Equation (4.2)
contents.result: The Fourier coefficients of a product are the discrete convolution of the coefficients.

contents.name: Theorem 4.2
contents.result: A(T) is closed under multiplication with the ell-1 norm estimate.

contents.name: Chapter 4 - Holder inclusion sentence
contents.result: C^alpha(T) lies in A(T) when alpha is greater than one half.

contents.name: Theorem 4.3
contents.result: A nowhere-zero member of A(T) has reciprocal in A(T).

contents.name: 3.3 Decay of Fourier Coefficients
contents.result: Relates regularity and coefficient decay.

contents.name: 3.3.1 Decay of Fourier Coefficients of Arbitrary Integrable Functions
contents.result: Introduces the Riemann--Lebesgue and arbitrarily-slow-decay results.

contents.name: Proposition 3.3.1 (Riemann--Lebesgue lemma)
contents.result: Fourier coefficients of an L1 torus function tend to zero.

contents.name: Lemma 3.3.2
contents.result: A null positive sequence has a dominating decreasing convex null sequence.
contents.reason: This auxiliary convex-sequence construction serves the source's arbitrary-slow-decay theorem, whereas neither planned proof uses that construction or conclusion.

contents.name: Lemma 3.3.3
contents.result: A weighted second-difference identity holds for a convex decreasing sequence.
contents.reason: The telescoping identity is used only in the source's slow-decay construction and does not occur in the chosen dyadic proof of the Holder threshold.

contents.name: Theorem 3.3.4
contents.result: For any prescribed null rate there is an L1 function with Fourier coefficients at least that large.
contents.reason: This produces integrable functions with arbitrarily slow coefficient decay, a different boundary question from the continuous endpoint example selected for this pair.

contents.name: 3.3.2 Decay of Fourier Coefficients of Smooth Functions
contents.result: Develops regularity-to-decay estimates and partial converses.

contents.name: Definition 3.3.5
contents.result: Defines the homogeneous Lipschitz seminorm and space for 0 < gamma < 1.

contents.name: Definition 3.3.6
contents.result: Defines the inhomogeneous Lipschitz norm and space.

contents.name: Remark 3.3.7
contents.result: The Lipschitz classes are continuous and distinguishes the norm from the homogeneous seminorm.

contents.name: Remark 3.3.8
contents.result: The homogeneous seminorm does not control the L-infinity norm without fixing constants.
contents.reason: The planned Bernstein statement uses a Hölder modulus for a fixed continuous function and makes no homogeneous-seminorm-only norm estimate.

contents.name: Theorem 3.3.9
contents.result: Derivatives and Hölder regularity give pointwise Fourier-coefficient decay.
contents.reason: This is a pointwise-decay theorem for classical derivatives, while the planned corollary uses a distinct L2 weak-derivative and finite-Bessel argument.

contents.name: Corollary 3.3.10
contents.result: Packages the derivative and Hölder coefficient-decay estimates with inhomogeneous weights.
contents.reason: Its inhomogeneous pointwise estimates are not invoked: the selected derivative criterion instead takes weighted ell-2 control into the separate Cauchy--Schwarz lemma.

contents.name: Remark 3.3.11
contents.result: Records the gamma = 1 endpoint convention for Lip1.

contents.name: Proposition 3.3.12
contents.result: Sufficient coefficient decay gives differentiability and Hölder regularity.
contents.reason: This reverse regularity implication is not needed to establish absolute convergence from regularity or to prove either selected boundary example.

contents.name: Definition 3.3.13
contents.result: Defines bounded variation on the one-dimensional torus.
contents.reason: Bounded variation supplies a separate O(1/|m|) decay route and is not a hypothesis, conclusion, or proof ingredient of the planned A/B pair.

contents.name: Proposition 3.3.14
contents.result: Bounded variation gives an O(1/|m|) Fourier-coefficient bound.
contents.reason: The page uses the sharp Holder threshold through dyadic square sums; adding the bounded-variation route would create an unused parallel criterion.

contents.name: Table 3.1 Interconnection between smoothness and Fourier coefficient decay
contents.result: Summarizes several decay scales.
contents.reason: The table surveys substantially more regularity classes than the two chosen sufficient criteria and its broad comparison is not a claim this pair needs.

contents.name: 3.3.3 Functions with Absolutely Summable Fourier Coefficients
contents.result: Introduces the absolute-convergence algebra and its sharp smoothness criterion.

contents.name: Definition 3.3.15
contents.result: Defines A(T^n) and its coefficient ell-1 norm.

contents.name: Theorem 3.3.16
contents.result: A Hölder condition above the dimension-half threshold implies absolute convergence.

contents.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3.16
contents.result: Uses dyadic frequency blocks, translation differences, finite orthogonality, and Cauchy--Schwarz.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.1
contents.result: Gives an alternate construction behind Lemma 3.3.2.
contents.reason: This is an alternate proof of a slow-decay auxiliary lemma, while the planned page neither invokes the slow-decay construction nor its convex-sequence machinery.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.2
contents.result: Builds a one-dimensional majorant for a multidimensional null sequence.
contents.reason: The exercise supports the source's multidimensional slow-decay theorem; the assigned page is one-dimensional and follows the stated Holder dyadic route.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.3
contents.result: Studies elementary convex-function and decreasing-integrable-function limits.
contents.reason: These real-variable limit exercises only motivate the prior convex-sequence argument and add no ingredient to the proposed Fourier-algebra proofs.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.4
contents.result: Compares homogeneous Lipschitz seminorms at two exponents.
contents.reason: The Bernstein proof fixes one exponent and chooses an intermediate sequence weight, so a full inter-exponent embedding theorem would not be used.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.5
contents.result: A differentiable function with derivative in L2(T) belongs to A(T).
contents.reason: The exercise assumes a classical differentiable function and its classical L2 derivative, while the planned corollary requires the unmaterialized torus weak-derivative definition and Fourier-coefficient identity owned by PDE-11.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.6(a)
contents.result: The product of two A(T^n) functions belongs to A(T^n) with the product estimate.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.6(b)
contents.result: The convolution of two L2 torus functions belongs to A(T^n).
contents.reason: This L2 convolution corollary is neither a premise nor a consequence of the selected Wiener-algebra, Bernstein, derivative, or example claims.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.7
contents.result: A lacunary series is Hölder but has no uniformly improved pointwise coefficient decay.
contents.reason: The endpoint failure is supplied directly by Exercise 3.3.8; this distinct lacunary coefficient-decay limitation does not enter that counterexample.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.8 - endpoint construction
contents.result: Assuming an exponential-sum estimate, constructs a Lambda^(1/2)(T) function outside A(T).

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.8 - continuity consequence
contents.result: Its Lambda^(1/2)(T) example is continuous while its coefficients are not in ell-1.

contents.name: 1. Fourier series - opening conventions (1.1-1.8)
contents.result: Sets torus Fourier coefficients, characters, and the normalized inner-product conventions.

contents.name: Proposition 1.1
contents.result: The Abel/Poisson regularizations converge in the stated function-space senses.

contents.name: Corollary 1.2
contents.result: Fourier inversion holds for smooth torus functions.
contents.reason: The planned synthesis lemma obtains only the coefficient identification it needs from uniform convergence and finite orthogonality, not a full smooth inversion theorem.

contents.name: Equations (1.43)-(1.48)
contents.result: The Fourier transform is unitary between L2(T^n) and ell-2(Z^n), with the character system orthonormal.

contents.name: Proposition 1.3
contents.result: C^ell regularity with ell greater than n/2 gives absolute Fourier convergence by Plancherel and Cauchy--Schwarz.

contents.name: Exercise 1
contents.result: The Fourier transform of convolution is the product of Fourier transforms.

contents.name: Exercise 2
contents.result: The Fourier coefficients of a product are the convolution of the coefficient sequences.

contents.name: Exercise 3
contents.result: Every Lipschitz function on the circle has an absolutely convergent Fourier series.

contents.name: Exercise 4
contents.result: The Riemann--Lebesgue lemma for L1(T^n).

contents.name: Exercise 5
contents.result: Represents partial sums using the Dirichlet kernel.
contents.reason: The current pair concerns absolute convergence and its algebra, not the ordinary partial-sum kernel or its pointwise convergence problem.

contents.name: Exercise 6
contents.result: A vanishing condition at a point forces convergence of ordinary partial sums there.
contents.reason: This local ordinary-convergence criterion lies outside the absolute-convergence route and is not used by either the algebra theorem or the examples.

contents.name: Exercise 7
contents.result: Local Lipschitz regularity gives local ordinary Fourier convergence.
contents.reason: It treats ordinary partial sums on intervals, whereas the planned Holder result is the different global ell-1 coefficient conclusion.

contents.name: Exercise 8
contents.result: Piecewise Lipschitz functions have ordinary partial-sum midpoint limits at jumps.
contents.reason: The jump-value theorem belongs to ordinary Fourier convergence and neither supplies nor is needed for the absolute convergence or Wiener inversion material.

contents.name: Exercise 9
contents.result: Computes the Fourier series of the Lipschitz function |theta| and evaluates the reciprocal-square sum.
contents.reason: This specific coefficient computation would be a separate numerical example and is not required for the selected polynomial or non-C2 examples.

contents.name: Exercise 10
contents.result: Develops Fourier coefficients of powers and truncated powers.
contents.reason: The power-function calculation is unrelated to the planned proof graph and would not be used to establish any claimed Wiener-algebra property.

contents.name: Exercise 11
contents.result: States the localization principle for uniformly convergent Fourier series.
contents.reason: Localization concerns ordinary uniform convergence on an interval, not coefficient absolute summability or the inverse-closed algebra property.

contents.name: Exercise 12
contents.result: Hölder continuity gives uniform convergence of the ordinary Fourier series.
contents.reason: Uniform ordinary convergence for every positive Holder exponent is weaker and differently scoped than the sharp alpha greater than one-half ell-1 conclusion.

contents.name: Exercise 13
contents.result: Asks for a modulus-of-continuity condition ensuring uniform ordinary convergence.
contents.reason: This broad ordinary-convergence question would require a separate Dini-type development and does not participate in the selected absolute-convergence arguments.

contents.name: Exercise 14
contents.result: Derives the Fejer kernel and Cesaro convergence in C(S1) and Lp(S1).

contents.name: 19.2 Application: Absolutely convergent Fourier series
contents.result: Identifies the Wiener algebra W of continuous circle functions with absolutely summable Fourier coefficients as the Gelfand representation of ell-1(Z).

contents.name: Theorem 19.9
contents.result: A nowhere-zero member of W has its continuous pointwise reciprocal in W, hence with absolutely convergent Fourier series.

contents.name: Remark 19.10
contents.result: Contrasts Wiener's original proof with the Gelfand proof and refers to a Neumann-series proof.
contents.reason: The assigned page records the inverse-closedness interface but neither compares historical proofs nor develops a separate Neumann-series proof of the reserved FA-18 theorem.

contents.name: Exercise 19.11
contents.result: Asks to prove that the Gelfand homomorphism from ell-1(Z) to C(S1) is not bounded below.
contents.reason: This norm-separation exercise does not enter the local Wiener-algebra spine or its blocked inversion interface, and would create a distinct functional-analysis detour.
